rows.name: CoverageGapDuringHandoverHazard
rows.text: If sector handover between two members is not make-before-break, the sector can go briefly unwatched while responsibility transfers between them.

rows.name: PositionDriftHazard
rows.text: without satellite positioning, a member's position estimate drifts and its reports place objects in the wrong place

rows.name: MeshJammingHazard
rows.text: interference cuts the links between members, and coordination stalls

rows.name: MisclassificationHazard
rows.text: a detection is reported as the wrong class, or a forced class where Unknown was the truth

rows.name: SensingDegradedUnnoticedHazard
rows.text: a sensor degrades and nobody knows the reports from it are unreliable

rows.name: StaleTrackHazard
rows.text: a track is shown as current after nothing has seen the object for a while

rows.name: SpoofedMemberHazard
rows.text: something that is not one of the members joins the mesh and takes part in coordination

rows.name: MixedClassifierVersionsHazard
rows.text: members run different classifier versions and classify the same object differently

rows.name: OperatorOverloadHazard
rows.text: more alerts reach the operator than they can judge, and they accept what is in front of them

rows.name: RecallWins
rows.text: RecallWins: once a drone is recalled, it does not watch again until it has landed

rows.name: ReturnsWhenIsolated
rows.text: ReturnsWhenIsolated: from any situation a drone can be in, it can always get back to landed, an isolated drone included

rows.name: GeofenceBreachEndsWatch
rows.text: GeofenceBreachEndsWatch: once a drone is outside its cleared airspace, it does not watch until it has landed

rows.name: QuarantinedStaysOut
rows.text: QuarantinedStaysOut: once a drone is quarantined, it takes no part in coordination until it has been readmitted

rows.name: PeerCoordinationSinglePointHazard
rows.text: a single point of failure this layer's intended split introduces: handOverSector, rotateRecharge and admitMember are each meant to be carried out by one member acting for its peers; if that member fails or drops out mid-exchange, the coordination step is left incomplete until another member takes over.

rows.name: GroundLinkC2SinglePathHazard
rows.text: accepted: the five #C2 functions are allocated only to mainComponent, the ground-facing boundary; a total GroundStationLink loss removes the supervisory command, recall and acknowledgement path until the link returns. Accepted because DisconnectedOperationAndReconciliation already keeps detectAndClassify and reportDetection running through the gap, and SafetyAuthority requires recall and geofence authority to stay independent of onboard software rather than delegated to the fleet.

rows.name: CoordinationDivergenceHazard
rows.text: with sector handover, recharge rotation and coverage redistribution decided independently by members rather than arbitrated by the ground, two members may reach conflicting local decisions at the same moment — e.g. both vacating the same sector for recharge — with no ground arbiter to break the tie

rows.name: GroundAdmissionBottleneckHazard
rows.text: accepted: because admitMember stays solely at the ground control station, a lost ground link blocks admission or readmission of any member until the link returns. This is deliberately fail-closed — an un-vetted candidate is safer excluded than admitted — and existing members' watch is unaffected since the other seven #Coordination functions run on board regardless of ground reachability

rows.name: GroundLinkRadioDropHazard
rows.text: the onboard or ground GroundLinkRadioUnitNode can drop, cutting a member from the ground-held deciding coordination it depends on in this alternative

rows.name: BatterySwapWearHazard
rows.text: the battery contacts and swap mechanism at rechargePoint wear with repeated twenty-minute-cycle swaps and can fail to seat a battery correctly

rows.name: OnboardComputeCrashHazard
rows.text: the onboard sensing and classification software can crash mid-sortie, silently stopping detection

rows.name: GroundCoordinatorSinglePointHazard
rows.text: concentrating the deciding Coordination and all Command-and-Control on groundStation.coordinator and groundStation.c2 makes their loss a fleet-wide coordination stall, a risk this ground-centred split creates that a drone-held one would not

rows.name: SurveillanceDroneAirframeItemContract
rows.text: the delivery contract for one drone airframe: bounded by the fleet size, endurance and cruise budgets the mission fixes

rows.name: fleetAirframeContract
rows.text: the instance of the airframe contract carried by each delivered unit of the fleet

rows.name: OnboardMissionSoftwareItemContract
rows.text: the build contract for the onboard software load: one baseline installed identically on every member, meeting the fleet's detection performance budget

rows.name: onboardSoftwareContract
rows.text: the instance of the software contract carried by each installed load

rows.name: ClassifierReleaseItemContract
rows.text: the release contract: exactly one classifier version is current across the fleet at any time, within the per-drone onboard compute cost budget

rows.name: classifierReleaseContract
rows.text: the instance of the release contract carried by the fielded classifier release

rows.name: RadioModuleItemContract
rows.text: the procurement contract for the radio module: carries mesh and ground-link traffic within the jammed-link share the brief assumes, with an approved equivalent substitutable for the primary part number

rows.name: radioModuleContract
rows.text: the instance of the radio module contract carried by each delivered unit

rows.name: GroundStationItemContract
rows.text: the delivery contract for the ground installation: hosts coordination, command and control, triage and the classifier registry within the fleet's report-delivery latency budget

rows.name: groundStationContract
rows.text: the instance of the ground station contract carried by the delivered installation

rows.name: RechargePointItemContract
rows.text: the delivery contract for the recharge point: swaps a battery and returns a member to flight within the fleet's turnaround budget

rows.name: rechargePointContract
rows.text: the instance of the recharge point contract carried by the delivered installation

rows.name: RecoveryPointItemContract
rows.text: the delivery contract for the recovery point: reachable and usable by any of up to the fleet's twelve members when isolated, per ReturnsWhenIsolated

rows.name: recoveryPointContract
rows.text: the instance of the recovery point contract carried by the delivered installation

rows.name: ClassifierReleaseVersionDriftHazard
rows.text: the classifier release procured for the fleet can drift into more than one version across the twelve installed copies if configuration control lapses between builds, independent of the behavioural MixedClassifierVersionsHazard already stated at SA

rows.name: RadioModuleSupplierDiscontinuationHazard
rows.text: the commercial supplier of the radio module can stop shipping the qualified part number, leaving no replacement for repair or fleet growth

rows.name: RechargePointPartObsolescenceHazard
rows.text: accepted: the battery-swap fixture's mechanical connector is a wear part from a narrow supplier base and may become obsolete over the programme's life; accepted because spares are stocked at procurement and the ground crew's per-cycle wear check, which satisfies BatterySwapWearHazard at PA, would catch a failing connector before it strands a member
